title: Unified prefix crediting for interleaved streaming requests
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary:
We observe inconsistent token crediting for interleaved or resumed streaming sessions where client-side retries, multiplexed connections, or partial resume semantics cause the metering pipeline to either double-credit prefixes or fail to credit resumed output. This ticket implements a unified prefix-crediting protocol and reconciliation hooks in the metering pipeline to guarantee deterministic per-request accounting across: (a) in-order streams, (b) out-of-order fragments, and (c) resumed/multiplexed streams with partial prefixes.

Problem details / root cause analysis:
- Current pipeline credits tokens by ingest order and uses best-effort dedupe by fragment timestamps. When clients resume a stream or send overlapping prefixes (e.g., mobile reconnect + server-side retries), fragments can be counted twice or missed.
- Streaming sidecars and gateway retries create divergent attribution: sidecar may attribute prefix->session A while the runtime binds the same KV cache to session B after failover, causing mismatch.
- Rate limiter and per-token quotas assume monotonically increasing token counts per session; out-of-order increments cause transient quota overshoots and incorrect throttling.
- Existing reconciliation jobs (daily) discover and correct some discrepancies but the window is large and customer-visible billing artifacts appear.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Protocol: define a compact session-fragment identity tuple (session_id, fragment_uuid, prefix_hash, fragment_index) that is produced by the gateway and passed through the serving runtime and metering sidecar. Tickets must include this tuple in streaming proto metadata for every emitted fragment.
2) Idempotent crediting: implement an at-most-once semantics in metering by using an LRU-backed fragment registry keyed by (session_id, fragment_uuid). Registry persists short-lived tombstones for N seconds equal to max resume window.
3) Prefix checkpointing: before emitting tokens, the runtime will checkpoint prefix totals at the gateway; on resume, gateway will include last_checkpoint_token_count to allow the metering pipeline to reconcile delta only.
4) Reconciliation extension: tighten the nearline reconciliation job to run hourly for streams with >x variance and include deterministic heuristics to merge partial credits using prefix_hash.
5) Rate limiter integration: modify quota checks to use session-level monotonic counters derived from reconciled checkpoints instead of raw ingest counters.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Performance: registry/tombstones add memory and write load to the sidecar path. We'll implement a size-limited LRU + probabilistic bloom filter to bound RAM; initial microbench shows ~5% adding to p50 latency under synthetic load (acceptable given P1 impact).
- Complexity: requires coordinated runtime/gateway/sidecar changes and a short compatibility window where both protocols are understood. We'll implement backwards-compatible fallback: if tuple metadata missing, fall back to current behavior and tag stream for aggressive reconciliation.
- Window length selection: too short -> duplicates for slow resumes; too long -> tombstone memory pressure. We'll start with 5 minutes and tune via canary telemetry.

Design & implementation tasks (high-level):
- Gateway: emit fragment metadata and last_checkpoint_token_count (PR: github.com/redwood/gateway/pull/789).
- Serving runtime: attach fragment_uuid and prefix_hash to fragments (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1332).
- Metering sidecar: implement fragment registry, idempotent crediting logic, and checkpoint reconciliation code path (this ticket).
- Nearline job: hourly reconciliation pipeline update and alerting rules (PR: github.com/redwood/metering/pull/456).
- E2E tests: new harness that simulates reconnects, multiplexing, and out-of-order fragments; property tests asserting per-session monotonic token counters.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests for idempotent crediting and registry behavior implemented and green in CI.
- Canary rollout (5% synthetic + internal traffic) shows no >0.5% delta between gateway checkpoint and metering counters after 30m for resumed streams.
- No regression in p50/p95 latency benchmarks beyond the accepted budget (+7% at p95 for sidecar).
- Reconciliation job can resolve >95% of detected anomalies within 2 hours for affected sessions.

Metrics to add / dashboards:
- metric:metering.fragment_dedupe_hits and fragment_dedupe_misses
- metric:metering.tombstone_evictions
- meter:metering.reconciliation_delta_percentile by stream_type
- Alert: Reconciliation failure rate >0.5% over 1h

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gates in gateway and runtime; sidecar defaults to conservative mode when tuple absent.
2) Deploy sidecar change to canary pool (5%) with synthetic reconnect scenarios.
3) Expand to internal traffic (alpha teams) for 72h, monitor dashboards and billing diffs.
4) Gradual 25/50/100% rollout with monitoring gates.

Backward compatibility:
- If gateway/runtimes do not provide metadata, sidecar uses legacy logic and labels stream for priority reconciliation. See fallback appendix in Confluence.
